# Ra.One – Summary
**Ra.One** is a 2011 Indian science-fiction superhero film directed by Anubhav Sinha, starring Shah Rukh Khan in a dual role as both the game programmer Shekhar Subramaniam and his digital creation, the protagonist G.One. Set in London, the story follows Shekhar’s quest to impress his son Prateek and wife Sonia by creating a video game with a villain more powerful than the hero. The antagonist, Ra.One, is a self-learning, shapeshifting AI who escapes from the digital world into reality and seeks to eliminate “Lucifer,” Prateek’s gaming alias. After Ra.One kills Shekhar and Shekhar’s colleague Akashi, Prateek and Sonia flee to India, protected by G.One, who also enters the real world. Ra.One pursues them relentlessly until G.One, with Prateek’s help, defeats him by exploiting Ra.One’s only weakness—his shadow. G.One returns to the digital world but is later restored to reality by Prateek.

# Production, Release, and Reception
Ra.One was produced by Red Chillies Entertainment, with significant investment in high-end visual effects and international collaboration on stunts and post-production. The film’s music was composed by Vishal-Shekhar and featured international artists like Akon. Ra.One set records for its marketing expenditure and wide release, including extensive digital promotions and a licensed video game tie-in. The film received a mixed critical reception in India and generally positive reviews overseas, earning praise for its technological achievements and visual effects, but criticism for its story and direction. Ra.One broke box office records in its opening days and became the highest-grossing Hindi film overseas in 2011, though its collections quickly fell. It garnered many awards, notably for its special effects, and sparked speculation about a sequel, though none has yet materialized. The film also faced controversies over plagiarism claims, cybertheft incidents, and cultural representation.
